feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8y=6{e}^{4x}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -8 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda -4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =-2$ or $\lambda =4$,  hence the complementary function ${y}_{c}$ is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{-2x}+B{e}^{4x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $6{e}^{4x}.$ In this case, the constant factor in the exponent is $4$, which coincides with one of the roots of the auxiliary equation. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha x{e}^{4x},
$$

where $\alpha $ is a constant that is to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=\alpha (1+4x){e}^{4x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=\alpha (8+16x){e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute ${y}_{p},$ ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and ${y}_{p}^{″}$ into the ODE and solve for $\alpha :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha (8+16x){e}^{4x}-2(\alpha (1+4x){e}^{4x})-8\alpha x{e}^{4x} & =6{e}^{4x} \\ (8+16x-2-8x-8x)\alpha {e}^{4x} & =6{e}^{4x} \\ 6\alpha {e}^{4x} & =6{e}^{4x} \\ 6\alpha  & =6 \\ \alpha  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=x{e}^{4x}.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{-2x}+B{e}^{4x}+x{e}^{4x}.
$$
